title: Synthetic example: why a cache needs a size limit
context: A newly scripted illustration for testing Synapse publication. This is not a real contributor conversation and contains no private submission material.
subject: Computer science

messages.text: If a cache makes lookups faster, why not let it keep everything?
A cache uses limited memory. Without a size limit, keeping more entries can consume memory needed by the rest of the application.
So reaching the limit should remove something, rather than refuse every new item?
That is one common choice. A least recently used policy removes the entry that has gone unused for the longest time, making room for a new entry. The best policy depends on the workload.
